title: UniProof: university credentials as PDAs, with registrar and dean sign-off
summary: A university account issues numbered credential PDAs to student wallets. A credential counts as valid once a registrar flag and a dean flag are both set and it isn't revoked, but the program never checks who sets those flags.
what: UniProof puts degrees on chain. A wallet creates one **University** PDA at `["university", wallet]`. Its authority issues **Credentials** at `["credential", university, n]` (n = the university's running counter) to any student wallet, with degree, field, graduation date and a metadata link. Each credential starts with `registrar_signed = false` and `dean_signed = false`. `sign_as_registrar` and `sign_as_dean` set those flags. `verify_credential` returns `registrar && dean && !revoked` as a bool. The authority can revoke. Students can record a **DisclosureProof** PDA saying they shared part of a credential. The access control is the lesson here: `issue` and `revoke` are properly locked with `has_one`, but the two signature instructions accept **anyone**, and our devnet run proves it.
app_note: The fork's own Next.js app (UniProof) as a static export with this devnet program ID. The fork imports `src/idl/uniproof.json` but doesn't commit it, so it was written from the committed TypeScript IDL type. The other changes are basePath, unoptimized images, and skipping lint at build. Pages: **/university/** (initialize, issue, sign), **/verify/** and **/student/**. There is no screen for revoking or for disclosure proofs. Script: [tests/devnet/chinesepowered-solana-cypherpunk.mjs](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/chinesepowered-solana-cypherpunk.mjs).

try_steps.do: Open [the app](/dapps/chinesepowered-solana-cypherpunk/), connect Phantom on **devnet** (0.05 devnet SOL is enough) and go to **University Portal** (/university/). Enter a University Name and press **Initialize University**.
try_steps.see: An `initialize_university` transaction. The page then shows University Information: your name, Credentials Issued 0, and the University Address, which is the PDA `["university", your wallet]`.
ran: Test wallet m4Ac…: Initialize University ("sol.college UI University")

try_steps.do: Issue a credential: Student Wallet Address = your own wallet (or a second one), Degree Type `Bachelor of Science`, Field of Study `Computer Science`, a Graduation Date, and an optional Metadata URI. Press **Issue Credential**.
try_steps.see: An `issue_credential` transaction. The dialog shows the new credential's address, `["credential", university, 0]`, and Credentials Issued becomes 1. On **/verify/** that address now reads **Unverified Credential**: no signatures yet.
ran: Issue Credential to its own wallet; the dialog showed credential FuuEaM9d…

try_steps.do: Under **Sign Credential (Multi-Sig)**, paste the credential address and press **Sign as Registrar**.
try_steps.see: A `sign_as_registrar` transaction. The program only checks that the credential isn't revoked; it doesn't care who you are.

try_steps.do: Press **Sign as Dean**, then open **/verify/** and **/student/**.
try_steps.see: A `sign_as_dean` transaction. /verify/ shows **Verified Credential**, and /student/ (when the credential is yours) lists it with ✓ Signed for both. The same wallet supplied both "independent" signatures.
ran: Sign as Dean; /verify/ showed Verified Credential and /student/ ✓ Signed twice

try_steps.do: Optional, with a second wallet: initialize its own university, then paste wallet 1's credential address into its **Sign as Registrar** box.
try_steps.see: It is accepted: `SignCredential` never links the credential to the university you pass, nor the signer to any role. We read this from the code; the script did the same with an unrelated wallet R and it was accepted (3N3CnFKr…).
ran: Script: unrelated wallet R signs as registrar on U's credential, accepted
try_steps.ran_note: Not clicked in the app with a second wallet; the program-level behaviour is what the script recorded.

diagram:
wallet U ─ initialize_university(name, authority) ─▶ University PDA ["university", U]   (name, authority, credentials_issued = n, bump)
U (has_one authority) ─ issue_credential(student, degree, field, date, uri) ─▶ Credential PDA ["credential", university, n]   n += 1
                                                                              registrar_signed = false, dean_signed = false
ANY signer ─ sign_as_registrar ─▶ registrar_signed = true     (only checks: not revoked)
ANY signer ─ sign_as_dean      ─▶ dean_signed = true
anyone ─ verify_credential (view) ─▶ registrar_signed && dean_signed && !is_revoked
U (has_one university + authority) ─ revoke_credential ─▶ is_revoked = true, revocation_date
student ─ create_disclosure_proof(credential_key, type, nonce) ─▶ DisclosureProof PDA ["disclosure", student, nonce]
accounts: Name (≤100), authority, is_active, credentials_issued (the counter used in credential seeds), bump
University, student, degree (≤50), field (≤100), graduation and issue dates, metadata URI (≤200), is_revoked, revocation_date, registrar_signed, dean_signed, bump
Credential key, student, disclosure type (DegreeOnly, DegreeAndField, DegreeAndDate, Full), timestamp, nonce

instructions.name: `initialize_university`: one per wallet, and a seed mismatch
steps: `init` with `seeds = [b"university", authority]`, where `authority` is the **Signer**, so a wallet can only have one; U's second attempt failed with "already in use".

The handler then stores the *argument* `authority`, which may be a different key. Every later instruction finds the university at `["university", university.authority]`, so if the two differ the account is unusable. Our script's X created a university naming U, and X's issue then failed with **ConstraintSeeds** (Exercise 3).
`#[derive(InitSpace)]` + `#[max_len]` sizes the account exactly, so the rent is small and fixed.

instructions.name: `issue_credential`: authority-gated, counter-numbered
steps: The credential's seeds include `university.credentials_issued` *before* the increment, so credentials are numbered 0, 1, 2… and each address is predictable.

`university` is re-derived from its stored authority (`seeds` + `bump = university.bump`) and `has_one = authority` requires that authority to sign. Our script's unrelated wallet R got **ConstraintHasOne**.
`issuer` (who pays) is a separate signer from `authority`; the app passes the same wallet for both. `is_active` is never checked.

instructions.name: `sign_as_registrar` / `sign_as_dean`: the missing check
steps: `SignCredential` asks for a credential, *a* university (checked only to be a real university PDA), and a `signer`. Nothing compares the signer with a registrar, a dean or the authority, and nothing says `credential.university == university`.
The only rule is `require!(!credential.is_revoked)`: after U revoked, R's signature got **CredentialRevoked**.
So the "multi-sig" is two booleans anyone can set. On devnet, R (unrelated) set `registrar_signed` on U's credential (3N3CnFKr…). After U's dean signature, `verify_credential` returned **true**.

instructions.name: `verify_credential`: a view function
steps: It returns `Result<bool>`, which Anchor writes as return data. A client can `simulate`/`.view()` it with no fee and no signature.
The script read **false** after the registrar only, **true** after both, and **false** after revocation.

instructions.name: `revoke_credential`: done right
steps: Two `has_one`s chain the checks: the credential's `university` field must be this university, and the university's `authority` must sign. R got **ConstraintHasOne**; U's revoke (36gFR1Yf…) succeeded.
This is the pattern the sign instructions should have used.

instructions.name: `create_disclosure_proof`: a record, not a proof
steps: The PDA `["disclosure", student, nonce]` makes each nonce single-use per student: reusing nonce 1 failed with "already in use".

`credential_key` is a plain argument, so it isn't checked to exist or to belong to the student (code reading). The credential data is public on chain anyway, so nothing is hidden. There's no zero-knowledge proof despite the "selective disclosure" name.

innovation.title: access control through account constraints
innovation.text: Everything this program gets right, it gets right in `#[derive(Accounts)]`: PDAs rebuilt from stored fields (`seeds = ["university", university.authority]`, `bump = university.bump`) and `has_one` links between accounts stop anyone issuing or revoking for a university they don't control. Everything it gets wrong is a constraint that's missing. Comparing `IssueCredential`/`RevokeCredential` with `SignCredential` side by side is the clearest lesson on Anchor authorization you'll find.
more: Fix it with roles: store `registrar` and `dean` keys on the University, then add `has_one = university` on the credential and a `constraint = signer.key() == university.registrar` (and dean) on `SignCredential`. Exercise 1 does exactly this.

Counter-numbered PDAs (`credentials_issued` in the seeds) let the app list a university's credentials without a list account. The app uses `memcmp` filters on the `university` (offset 8) or `student` (offset 40) field instead.

frontend.title: One client class for all instructions
steps: `getCredentialPDA` encodes the index as 8 little-endian bytes, matching `to_le_bytes()` in the seeds.
Before issuing it fetches the university's `credentialsIssued` to derive the next credential address, and refuses if that address already exists.

frontend.title: Signing passes *your* university
steps: `signAsRegistrar(credential, universityPDA)` uses the connected wallet's own university and the pasted credential address. The program doesn't check they belong together, which is why step 5 works.

frontend.title: Verify reads the account, not the view
steps: The app recomputes `registrarSigned && deanSigned && !isRevoked` from a plain account fetch instead of calling `verify_credential`. It gets the same answer for free.
/student/ lists your credentials with `credential.all([{memcmp: {offset: 40, bytes: wallet}}])`.

exercises.title: Give the signatures real roles
steps: Add `registrar: Pubkey` and `dean: Pubkey` to University (set in `initialize_university`).
In `SignCredential`: `#[account(mut, has_one = university)] credential`, and split it into `SignAsRegistrar` with `constraint = signer.key() == university.registrar` and `SignAsDean` with the dean.
Optionally require registrar ≠ dean.
exercises.expect: Replaying the script, R's registrar signature fails with a constraint error instead of succeeding as 3N3CnFKr… did, and a credential only verifies after both named people sign.
exercises.hint: The University account is the natural place to store `registrar` and `dean` pubkeys, set at `initialize_university`.
exercises.approach: Add those two fields, then split `SignCredential` into two structs with `has_one = university` on the credential and `constraint = signer.key() == university.registrar` (and dean). Replaying the script, R's registrar signature should fail a constraint instead of succeeding as 3N3CnFKr… did, and a credential should only verify after both named people sign.

exercises.title: Stop cross-university signing
steps: With only `has_one = university` added (no roles yet), try step 5 again: wallet 2 signs wallet 1's credential while passing wallet 2's university.
exercises.expect: ConstraintHasOne: the credential's university field doesn't match the university passed.
exercises.hint: You can do this without roles: `has_one = university` alone stops a signer from passing a different university.
exercises.approach: Add `has_one = university` on the credential in `SignCredential`. Wallet 2 signing wallet 1's credential while passing wallet 2's university should then fail ConstraintHasOne.

exercises.title: Fix initialize_university's authority
steps: Drop the `authority: Pubkey` argument and store `ctx.accounts.authority.key()`, or seed the PDA from the argument and require that key to sign.
exercises.expect: The script's X → U case can no longer create an unusable university. X's issue no longer fails with ConstraintSeeds, because X's university now names X.
exercises.hint: The PDA is seeded by the *signer*, then the handler stores the *argument*. Those must be the same key.
exercises.approach: Drop the `authority: Pubkey` argument and store `ctx.accounts.authority.key()`, or seed the PDA from the argument and require that key to sign. The script's X→U case should no longer create an unusable university, and X's issue should no longer fail ConstraintSeeds.

exercises.title: Make disclosure proofs check the credential
steps: Replace `credential_key: Pubkey` with a `credential: Account<Credential>` with `constraint = credential.student == student.key()` and `!credential.is_revoked`.
Add a Disclosure screen on /student/.
exercises.expect: A student can only record a disclosure for their own, unrevoked credential. Using someone else's credential (or a random key) is rejected.
exercises.hint: `credential_key` is a raw `Pubkey` argument, so the program never loads the credential. Make it an account instead.
exercises.approach: Replace the argument with `credential: Account<Credential>` and `constraint = credential.student == student.key()` plus `!credential.is_revoked`. A student recording a disclosure for someone else's credential (or a random key) should be rejected. Then add a Disclosure screen on /student/.

exercises.title: Add revoke and status to the app
steps: On /university/, list the university's credentials with `getUniversityCredentials` and add a **Revoke** button calling `revokeCredential`.
Check `is_active` in `issue_credential` and add an instruction for the authority to deactivate the university.
exercises.expect: Revoking from the app turns /verify/ to Credential Revoked, as U's scripted revoke (36gFR1Yf…) did, and a deactivated university can't issue.
exercises.hint: The client already has `revokeCredential` and `getUniversityCredentials`. The university page just doesn't call them.
exercises.approach: List the university's credentials and add a Revoke button. After a revoke, /verify/ should show Credential Revoked, as U's scripted revoke (36gFR1Yf…) did. Optionally check `is_active` in `issue_credential` and add a deactivate instruction.

not_covered: Initialize, issue, both signatures, verify and the student list were clicked through in the app. Outsider signing, revocation, disclosure proofs, the authority-mismatch university and every rejected case were run by script. Not exercised: issuing to a different student wallet from the app, create_disclosure_proof with someone else's credential key (read from code).
objectives: Compare two instruction structs side by side: `issue` and `revoke` locked with `has_one`, and `SignCredential` with a signer that is never compared to a role.
Use a counter-numbered PDA (`["credential", university, n]`) and walk a university's credentials.
Explain a seed mismatch: a university stored a different authority than the key it was derived from, and became unusable.
prereqs: Phantom on devnet and about 0.05 SOL.
[Friendstake](/lessons/friendstake/) immediately before this: you have just seen a missing `has_one` on a payee. Here the same idea is about *who may set a flag*.

build.note: `Cargo.toml` pins `anchor-lang` 0.31.1 (the `Anchor.toml` comment says 0.30.1; use the Cargo version). Tests: `tests/uniproof.ts`.
